# The pg_sage rubric

Rubric version: `pg_sage-rubric/1`. A change to the table below bumps the version, and a grade names the version it was computed with.

Licence: this rubric is published under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International licence (CC BY 4.0, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Anyone may grade a database with it, by hand or with another tool, and say so. The licence is the owner's decision; CC BY 4.0 is the stated default until it is made.

pg_sage grades a database against this rubric in code, read-only, with no model. [Sage Review](review.md) explains the reasoning behind each check; this page is generated from the table the code runs.

## Check results

A check that could not run is `unknown`: it stays in the denominator and adds nothing, so it can only lower a grade, never raise it.

| Result | Counts |
|---|---|
| `pass` | its full weight |
| `warn` | half its weight |
| `fail` | nothing |
| `unknown` | nothing, and stays in the denominator |
| `not_applicable` | leaves the denominator; only the platform decides it |

## Grade arithmetic

- Dimension score: passed weight over applicable weight, in percent.
- Coverage: applicable weight that ran (pass, warn or fail) over applicable weight.
- A dimension below 60% coverage has an `unknown` letter; its score is still kept.
- A critical check that failed, or could not show that it passed, caps its dimension at D.
- Overall score: the mean score of every dimension with applicable weight, known or not.
- Overall letter: `unknown` with fewer than 4 dimensions known; otherwise the overall score's letter, never more than one letter above the worst dimension's.

| Letter | Score from |
|---|---|
| A | 90 |
| B | 80 |
| C | 70 |
| D | 60 |
| F | 0 |

## What each source reports

| Source | What it reads | `pass` | `warn` | `fail` | `unknown` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `finding` | open findings of a category | no open finding, and the producer has run for the database | only info-severity findings are open | a warning or critical finding is open | the producer has not run for the database (cloud backup checks have no run record, so they are unknown unless a finding is open) |
| `firstlook` | a first-look catalog rule | the newest first look reports the rule ok | every item the rule reports is info | the rule reports a finding | the rule was degraded or did not run, or the first look finished more than 7 days ago |
| `posture` | an agent posture detector of the first look | the detector reports ok | every item the detector reports is info | the detector reports a finding | the detector was degraded or did not run, or the first look is more than 7 days old |
| `lint` | a schema lint rule, scanned live and read-only | the rule reports nothing | never | the rule reports an object | schema lint is off, the rule is in `schema_lint.disabled_rules`, or its catalog read failed |
| `runway` | a forecaster category | no open finding, and a forecaster snapshot over a day old exists | only info-severity findings are open | a warning or critical finding is open | the forecaster has less than a day of history |
| `drill` | the restore drill history | a restore drill passed in the last 35 days | the newest pass is older than 35 days | the newest drill failed, or no drill ever passed | no restore drill has run yet |
| `setting` | a server setting, read with one bounded probe | no setting waits for a restart; the server's major is supported | a setting waits for a restart; the major ends its life within 90 days | the major is past its end of life | the `pg_settings` probe (5 s `statement_timeout`) failed |
| `upgrade` | upgrade readiness, for a major at or near end of life | the readiness case has run and found nothing open | only info-severity readiness findings are open | a warning or critical readiness finding is open | `pg_settings` could not be read, or the readiness case has not run |

## Dimensions

8 dimensions. A check with platforms applies only there and is `not_applicable` elsewhere; a check that needs `cost.rates` is `unknown` without operator-supplied rates.
